chunks: The Quran has spoken of the story of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), that his mother gave birth to him in secrecy and hid him in the cave until he grew up, and then his story unraveled.

And regarding the story of Musa (peace be upon him), his mother cast him into the river fearing for his life and being cautious from Pharaoh (peace be upon him); this is well-known and mentioned by the Quran.
The story of the Master of the Age (peace be upon him) is similar to that; so how can it be said that this is outside of ordinary customs?
And among people is one who has a child from a concubine whom he hides from his wife for a period of time, until when death approaches him, he acknowledges him.

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الزَّمَانِ: Master of the Age (referring to the Twelfth Imam)

ai.seo_question: What Quranic examples support the concealed birth of the Imam of the Time?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi employs a comparative argument (qiyas) to refute skeptics by linking the hidden birth of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) to the Quranic narratives of Ibrahim and Musa, where divine protection necessitated concealment. He further grounds this in common human experience (al-'ada) by citing the practice of fathers acknowledging children born to concubines in secret, thereby demonstrating that such events are consistent with natural customs rather than being extraordinary anomalies.
